A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VibeCheck research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–H support comparison, including matching content across figure removals and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original VibeCheck evaluations, including model-matching and preference-prediction results in Table 2, application results in Section 6, and per-vibe results in Appendix G.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical evaluations in Table 2, Section 6, and Appendix G.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix D retain the same discovery, reduction, judge-based validation, filtering, logistic prediction, and error-driven iteration procedures. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HC3, Chatbot Arena overall/STEM/writing, CNN/DailyMail summarization, MATH reasoning, and COCO captioning using ShareGPT-4V captions. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the Predefined Vibes baseline and the same one- and three-iteration VibeCheck comparisons. The evaluated model pairings in Table 4 and predefined axes in Appendix C are unchanged.

E3.justification: Train/test counts, hyperparameters, metrics, preference-label generation, and filtering procedures are unchanged, including the MATH restriction to mutually correct answers. The shortened HC3 descriptions do not establish a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The iteration comparison, STEM-versus-writing analysis, judge-failure examples in Appendix F, and qualitative examples in Appendix H are retained. Removing the main-text summarization plot does not remove its analysis, which remains in Appendix G.

E5.justification: The regression/p-value discussion and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The CNN/DailyMail preference-coefficient profile reverses direction between v4 Figure 15 and v6 Figure 14 under unchanged axis definitions: conclusion strength, example specificity, and viewpoint coverage switch from negative to positive, while emotional tone switches from positive to negative. This substantially changes the reported preference associations, although accuracy results remain unchanged. The STEM caption also corrects nine discovered vibes to seven, matching the retained seven rows.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same formal vibe definition, separability formula, and prediction formulations. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and application claims, including the stated 80% model-identity and 61% preference-prediction accuracies.

C2.justification: Appendix B drops the quoted RLHF explanations and strengthens the HC3 description from ChatGPT expressing less emotion to not expressing emotions. The principal interpretations and limitations in Sections 5–7 remain unchanged, including the summarization discussion despite the reversed coefficient signs.

D1.justification: Appendix B replaces exact HC3 gold-standard descriptions with abridged summaries, reducing the reference-label detail available for checking human alignment. Implementation prompts, hyperparameters, dataset statistics, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix E are unchanged. The Chiquier et al. and GLUE reference edits update publication metadata rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: Appendix B is condensed and rewritten, acknowledgments become a shorter unnumbered paragraph, and conference headers and small caption edits are introduced. The main scientific narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v6 removes the main-text top-five summarization display while retaining the full appendix plot, places the math plot beside its discussion, enlarges and reflows Table 6, and adjusts figure spacing and captions. These are limited presentation changes rather than a wholesale redesign.

improvement.justification: The corrected STEM count and more readable Table 6 improve clarity. However, the unexplained summarization coefficient reversal leaves Section 6.1 unreconciled with the newly negative emotional-tone coefficient, and Appendix B loses exact reference detail while strengthening an emotion claim. The PDFs do not establish whether the coefficient reversal corrects an error or introduces one, preventing a reliable judgment of the net quality change.
